title: The Green Book: UK government guidance on appraisal - appraisal process, Five Case Model, key concepts and parameters
description: Machine-readable extract of the 2026 Green Book: the four-stage appraisal process, the Five Case Model (what each case contains and must demonstrate), business case stages (SOC/OBC/FBC), key appraisal concepts with paragraph references, and numeric appraisal parameters actually stated in the 2026 text. Values deferred to supplementary guidance are listed under parameters.not_in_edition and must be supplied by users. Crown copyright 2026, Open Government Licence v3.0.

extraction.method: Manual reading of the full 2026 text; each item anchored by regex to a unique body page of `pdftotext -layout` output; parameters parsed by regex and asserted (scripts/extract/greenbook.py).
extraction.notes: Item texts paraphrase the cited paragraphs; para numbers are those printed in the 2026 edition. Printed page = PDF page - 6 for body pages (verified from folios).

items.title: Who must follow the Green Book
items.text: Mandatory for UK government departments and arm's length bodies, with the accompanying business case guidance, when developing proposals involving significant public spending; also used for regulatory impact assessments.

items.title: Proportionality
items.text: Guidance should be used proportionately: effort should correlate with the proposal's scale, cost, complexity and risk.

items.title: Supplementary guidance
items.text: Many topics are covered in more detail in supplementary guidance listed on GOV.UK; departmental supplementary guidance is peer-reviewed by the Chief Economist Appraisal Group.

items.title: Appraisal versus evaluation
items.text: Appraisal assesses a proposal before approval; evaluation assesses it after implementation (Magenta Book). Consider from the outset how the proposal will be evaluated.

items.title: ROAMEF cycle
items.text: A proposal typically progresses through Rationale, Objectives, Appraisal, Monitoring, Evaluation and Feedback (ROAMEF). The Green Book focuses on the first three.

items.title: Social value
items.text: Social value is the value a proposal brings to UK residents: all benefits, costs and risks affecting wellbeing (prosperity, justice, security, climate, environment, health, distributional effects), not just financial returns.

items.title: Definition of value for money (Box 1)
items.text: Value for money is a balanced judgement on the optimal use of public resources, based on: performance against objectives and CSFs (options failing objectives cannot be VfM); monetisable costs and benefits; unmonetisable costs and benefits; public sector financial impact; distribution across groups and places; and risk and uncertainty.

items.title: Fraud risk
items.text: Pay particular attention to fraud risk where public money is distributed through grants, loans or other payments (Government Fraud Risk Assessment Standard).

items.title: Stage 1: Rationale and objectives
items.text: Set out why government needs to act, what is needed to bring about the desired outcomes, and what would happen if government does not act; establish specific objectives.

items.title: Stage 2: Generating options and longlist appraisal
items.text: Generate and assess a wide range of possible options for achieving the objectives; take the most compelling forward as a shortlist.

items.title: Stage 3: Shortlist appraisal
items.text: Detailed analysis of the shortlisted options using social cost-benefit analysis or social cost-effectiveness analysis.

items.title: Stage 4: Identifying the preferred option
items.text: Identify a single preferred option that optimises value for money and present it, with details of the appraisal process, in advice to decision makers.

items.title: All stages informed by evidence
items.text: All four stages must be informed by evidence, including previous evaluations of similar interventions; sources of uncertainty should be clearly communicated.

items.title: Strategic case
items.text: Sets out the rationale and objectives for the intervention.
items.demonstrates: The case for change and the SMART objectives the intervention will achieve.

items.title: Economic case
items.text: Sets out the longlist and shortlist of options for achieving the objectives in the strategic case and identifies the preferred option that delivers the best value for money.
items.demonstrates: The preferred option optimises value for money among a genuine range of options.

items.title: Commercial case
items.text: Describes how government will source the inputs required for delivering the preferred option and who will manage the risks associated with delivery and operation.
items.demonstrates: The preferred option can be sourced on commercially viable terms with appropriate risk allocation.

items.title: Financial case
items.text: Concerned with the affordability of the proposal for the public bodies involved.
items.demonstrates: The proposal is affordable and funded for every public body involved.
contents: Public sector costs in RDEL, CDEL or AME
Impact on income, expenditure and balance sheet of public bodies

items.title: Management case
items.text: Sets out the practical arrangements for implementation and demonstrates that the preferred option can be delivered successfully.
items.demonstrates: The preferred option can be delivered successfully.
contents: Change management, benefits realisation and risk management arrangements

items.title: Five cases developed together
items.text: The five dimensions are not five separate business cases but interconnected perspectives developed together iteratively and proportionately; no additional 'case' should be invented for special features (express them as objectives, CSFs or social costs/benefits).

items.title: Strategic Outline Case (SOC)
items.text: First stage: makes the case for change, identifies SMART objectives and sets out an initial longlist and shortlist of options to identify a preferred way forward.

items.title: Outline Business Case (OBC)
items.text: Second stage: revisits the SOC options to identify the preferred option after more detailed analysis, and outlines commercial, financial and management arrangements.

items.title: Full Business Case (FBC)
items.text: Third stage: sets out the full commercial, financial and management arrangements required to deliver the project successfully, following procurement.
appraisal_stages: Review and iterate the appraisal following the procurement process

items.title: Environmental principles policy statement (EPPS) duty
items.text: Environment Act 2021 duty on Ministers to have due regard to the EPPS; identify environmental effects of options and apply the five principles; reflect explicitly at longlist and shortlist stages.

items.title: Biodiversity duty
items.text: Public authorities in England must consider what they can do to conserve and enhance biodiversity; reflect explicitly at longlist and shortlist stages.

items.title: Public sector equality duty (PSED)
items.text: Have due regard to eliminating conduct prohibited by the Equality Act 2010, advancing equality of opportunity and fostering good relations; assess differential impacts on people with protected characteristics and consider mitigation.

items.title: Case for change
items.text: Explains why the government needs to act, why the outcomes are worth pursuing, why government is best placed, and why businesses, households and charities cannot achieve them themselves.

items.title: Market failure and equity rationales
items.text: Rationales include market failures (public goods, externalities, market power, imperfect information, co-ordination failure) and equity; PESTLE analysis can frame context.

items.title: Theory of change
items.text: The logical chain from inputs to outputs to outcomes, with stated, evidenced assumptions agreed by decision makers.

items.title: Business as usual (BAU)
items.text: The outcome expected if current arrangements continue and the proposal is not implemented; a benchmark. BAU does not mean doing nothing and must be fair and reasonable.

items.title: Present options in absolute terms
items.text: Costs and benefits should usually be presented in absolute terms rather than as increments from BAU; avoid normalising BAU to zero.

items.title: Deadweight and additionality
items.text: Deadweight: outcomes that would have happened anyway. Additionality: outcomes caused by the intervention.

items.title: SMART objectives
items.text: Objectives must be specific, measurable, achievable, realistic and time-limited; few in number; ideally outcome-based rather than output-based.

items.title: Strategic fit
items.text: Alignment with the higher-level programme/portfolio/policy, other proposals of the originating organisation and those of other public bodies.

items.title: Transformational change
items.text: Claims of transformational change (radical, permanent, qualitative change, often with tipping points and feedback) must be transparently explained and supported by evidence.

items.title: Policy hierarchy and golden thread
items.text: Objectives cascade from policy to portfolio, programme and project (the 'golden thread'); a project appraisal need not justify its parent programme.

items.title: CSF 1: Objectives and strategic fit
items.text: The proposal meets its SMART objectives and has strategic fit with other public sector activity.

items.title: CSF 2: Value for money
items.text: The proposal represents the optimal use of public resources to achieve its objectives.

items.title: CSF 3: Supplier capacity and capability
items.text: Suppliers can feasibly provide the inputs; government and suppliers can agree payments and risk transfer.

items.title: CSF 4: Affordability
items.text: The proposal is affordable for all of the public bodies involved.

items.title: CSF 5: Achievability
items.text: Robust arrangements are in place to deliver, monitor and evaluate the proposal.

items.title: Constraints as CSFs
items.text: CSFs may include constraints such as legal requirements, ethical standards, social acceptability, timing and environmental policy.

items.title: Longlist: options generation and longlist appraisal
items.text: Generate a wide range of options and assess them against objectives and CSFs to narrow to a shortlist; options failing objectives or CSFs must not proceed.

items.title: Document longlist reasoning
items.text: Document which options were considered and why each was or was not progressed to the shortlist.

items.title: Indicative estimates at longlist
items.text: Longlist appraisal typically uses indicative estimates and ranges rather than detailed CBA.

items.title: Dependencies and unintended consequences
items.text: Consider external dependencies and potential unintended consequences (e.g. gaming of incentive schemes).

items.title: Options framework filter (OFF)
items.text: Recommended (not mandatory) method: break options into components, rate option choices and recombine them; delivered through structured facilitated workshops with explicit deliberation.

items.title: OFF categories
items.text: Five recommended categories: scope, solution, delivery, implementation and funding, considered in that order.

items.title: OFF ratings (green/amber/red)
items.text: Green: best meets CSFs; amber: meets CSFs less well (both carried forward); red: fails CSFs (dropped). Record the reason for each rating with evidence, assumptions and sources.

items.title: MCDA acceptable; simple MCA not recommended
items.text: MCDA with swing weighting and an expert facilitator may be used; simple weighting-and-scoring MCA is recommended against. SWOT may also be used.

items.title: Options summary matrix
items.text: Present OFF results in an options summary matrix (categories, BAU, option choices, ratings) accompanied by a record of workshop decisions and rationale.

items.title: Shortlist composition (around five options)
items.text: Around five options: BAU, do minimum, preferred way forward, more ambitious and less ambitious preferred way forward (the latter may be excluded if the preferred way forward is the do minimum).

items.title: BAU always shortlisted
items.text: Options not achieving objectives must not be shortlisted, except BAU, which must always be taken forward as the benchmark.

items.title: Do minimum
items.text: The option that just achieves the objectives; shows whether other options add genuinely worthwhile improvements or 'gold plating'.

items.title: Preferred way forward vs preferred option
items.text: Longlist appraisal identifies a preferred way forward; shortlist appraisal identifies the preferred option, which may differ.

items.title: CBA or CEA
items.text: Social cost-benefit analysis (recommended for detailed comparison) or social cost-effectiveness analysis (when main benefits are unmonetisable or options deliver the same output differently).

items.title: Scope is UK society
items.text: Scope is all UK residents; consider impacts on other public bodies, households, businesses and charities, not just the originating organisation.

items.title: Time horizon
items.text: Cover the whole lifetime of the proposal. Standard horizons additional to year 0: 60 years infrastructure, 30 years refurbishment, 10 years regulations, 10 years other; agree longer periods with HM Treasury where effects extend beyond 60 years.

items.title: Year 0
items.text: Year 0 is generally the first year with social costs or benefits; may be standardised to a calendar or financial year across options.

items.title: Climate scenarios
items.text: Horizons ending before 2040: appraise against a 2C warming scenario; ending 2040 or later: at least 2C and 4C scenarios (AECC supplementary guidance).

items.title: Classifying costs and benefits
items.text: Monetisable (cash / non-cash) vs unmonetisable (quantifiable / qualitative); monetise where possible and proportionate, focusing on decisive impacts.

items.title: Capital, operating and maintenance costs
items.text: Distinguish capital, operating and maintenance costs; appraisals must reflect maintenance needed to sustain benefits.

items.title: Exclude sunk costs
items.text: Sunk costs must not be included; consider the opportunity cost of continuing to use already-paid resources.

items.title: Economic transfers
items.text: Transfers (taxes, grants, subsidies, benefits, fines) net to zero for society; either include as offsetting items (pushes BCR towards one) or exclude, and explain; must be shown in distributional analysis and public sector financial impact.

items.title: No GDP/GVA or Keynesian multipliers
items.text: Do not compare options on GDP/GVA changes and do not count Keynesian multiplier effects as social benefits.

items.title: Costs of raising public funds
items.text: Generally not included in appraisal, except when assessing private finance model options (Annex A).

items.title: Real prices
items.text: Estimate in real prices (nominal equals real in year 0): forecast nominal prices then remove general inflation using the GDP deflator.

items.title: GDP deflator forecasts
items.text: Five-year GDP deflator forecasts: latest OBR Economic and Fiscal Outlook; fifty-year: OBR Long-term economic determinants. (No deflator values are given in the Green Book.)

items.title: Relative price effects
items.text: Include significant relative price effects (e.g. construction) in CBA; quality changes may be reflected in real prices.

items.title: Social Time Preference Rate (STPR)
items.text: STPR is 3.50% real for years 1 to 30, 3.00% for years 31 to 75, and 2.50% for year 76 onwards. Derivation is in the supplementary guidance on discounting.

items.title: Applying discount factors
items.text: Multiply future-year values by that year's discount factor; pre-calculated factors are in the supplementary guidance on discounting (Table 8 gives a worked example).

items.title: Discount real values only
items.text: The STPR is a real rate and must be applied only to real values; never add inflation and discount rates together.

items.title: Health discount rate
items.text: Health and life effects are discounted at 1.5% (wealth effect excluded); the health rate applies in every year of the appraisal; other effects use the standard STPR.

items.title: No retrospective discounting
items.text: Do not discount (or compound) costs and benefits that have already occurred.

items.title: Risk and uncertainty
items.text: Must be considered as part of the VfM judgement. Uncertainty: assumptions not fully known; risk: the effect of uncertainty on objectives (consistent with the Orange Book).

items.title: Risk costs
items.text: Impact costs, correction costs and prevention costs; include risk costs in appraisal.

items.title: Risk mitigation and transfer
items.text: Weigh the costs and benefits of mitigation and of transferring risk to the party best able to manage it.

items.title: Contingent liabilities
items.text: Appraise contingent liabilities as part of the expected social cost of risk (HM Treasury contingent liability approval framework).

items.title: Expressing uncertainty
items.text: Central estimate and range; expected values (probability-weighted); confidence intervals; P90 values; consider tail risks proportionately.

items.title: Advanced risk methods
items.text: Scenario analysis, decision trees, real options analysis and Monte Carlo analysis for higher-cost, higher-risk proposals.

items.title: Optimism bias
items.text: Must explicitly adjust at the outset: increase costs and durations and decrease benefits. Size the adjustment from the organisation's historical forecast errors; if none, use generic values in the Green Book supplementary guidance on optimism bias (no percentages are given in the 2026 Green Book itself). Reduce the adjustment in proportion to risks prevented.

items.title: Contingency
items.text: Contingency (financial case) = remaining optimism bias adjustment + value of unprevented risk, converted to nominal; typically not allocated to the project because government self-insures. Prevention costs belong in core costs.

items.title: Public sector financial impact
items.text: Lifetime costs and receipts for all public bodies, excluding wider social costs; shown in nominal, undiscounted terms; cost-shifting within the public sector is not VfM.

items.title: Economic vs financial case treatment (Table 9)
items.text: Economic case: real, discounted at STPR, transfers optional, wider social impacts included. Financial case: nominal, undiscounted, transfers always included, wider social impacts excluded; depreciation only in the financial dimension.

items.title: PVB, PVC, PVC public, PVC non-public
items.text: Present values (real, discounted) of monetisable benefits (PVB), costs (PVC), public sector financial costs (PVC public) and costs outside the public sector (PVC non-public).

items.title: Net present social value (NPSV)
items.text: NPSV = PVB - PVC.

items.title: Benefit-cost ratio (BCR)
items.text: BCR = PVB / PVC: monetisable social benefits per pound of monetisable social cost.

items.title: Return on public sector cost (RPSC)
items.text: RPSC = (PVB - PVC non-public) / PVC public: social value relative to cost to the public sector.

items.title: Net present unit cost (NPUC)
items.text: For CEA: PVC relative to quantifiable (non-monetisable) social benefits.

items.title: Sign convention affects BCR
items.text: Treating an impact as a negative benefit or a cost changes the BCR (not NPSV or RPSC); explain the choice. Use a consistent approach across similar decisions.

items.title: Initial ranking is not sufficient
items.text: Rank options by summary metrics as a first step only; a single metric is not enough for the balanced VfM judgement (Box 1).

items.title: No BCR thresholds
items.text: Do not judge VfM using BCR thresholds (e.g. rejecting a proposal with BCR below two). A BCR below one may still be VfM if there are significant unmonetisable benefits, subject to rigorous scrutiny.

items.title: Compare options with the same objectives only
items.text: Summary metrics compare options meeting the same objectives, not proposals with different objectives.

items.title: Sensitivity analysis
items.text: Stress-test uncertain assumptions (e.g. input costs, demand) and show effects on social value.

items.title: Switching values
items.text: The value a key variable must reach for an option to stop being VfM (e.g. NPSV negative, or preferred option overtaken). At minimum, sensitivity analysis and switching values for the preferred option must be included in results; can also test unmonetisable benefits.

items.title: Proportionate distributional analysis
items.text: Effort proportionate to scale: describe small effects; analyse significant effects; present welfare effects where redistribution is an objective or effects are highly significant.

items.title: Income equivalisation
items.text: Adjust household incomes for composition (Figure 7 scores: first adult 0.67, additional adult 0.33, child 14+ 0.33, child under 14 0.20).

items.title: Distributional (welfare) weights
items.text: Welfare weight = (national median equivalised income / group median equivalised income)^1.3; weighted impact = income change x weight; weighted estimates must be shown alongside unweighted.

items.title: Place-based analysis
items.text: Assess distribution across places; consider additionality, deadweight, displacement, substitution and leakage; sub-national metrics always alongside UK-wide values.

items.title: Distributing money to local authorities
items.text: Follow the funding simplification doctrine; choose allocation or competition; competitive processes run bids to OBC with final allocation conditional on a satisfactory FBC.

items.title: Opportunity cost and market prices
items.text: Value at opportunity cost, starting from market prices excluding taxes and subsidies; use non-market valuation where markets fail.

items.title: Valuation hierarchy
items.text: From most to least reliable: market prices, generic prices, revealed preference, then stated preference / wellbeing valuation; use ranges and sensitivity for non-market prices.

items.title: Residual value
items.text: Include an asset's residual value or liability at the end of the appraisal period.

items.title: Full displacement of jobs
items.text: Assume no increase in national labour supply; any exception needs compelling evidence signed off by the chief economist.

items.title: Life and health values
items.text: Use VPF (TAG data book), SLY/VOLY and QALY (supplementary guidance on health); values are not given in the Green Book.

items.title: Energy use and GHG emissions
items.text: Value changes in energy use (quantity x LRVC) and emissions (quantity x emissions factor x social value of carbon) per DESNZ supplementary guidance; report levels and monetised values.

items.title: Negligible emissions threshold
items.text: Generally negligible if below 0.1 MtCO2e in every year of the appraisal horizon; basic analysis still required.

items.title: Natural capital screening
items.text: Screen options against natural capital assets; if any apply, follow the ENCA four-step approach.

items.title: Efficiency savings, fraud and error
items.text: Efficiency savings must not come from reduced outputs; treat fraud proceeds as a one-sided transfer or a social cost; assume fraud where error status is doubtful.

items.title: Business case executive summary
items.text: Spending appraisals are presented in a business case beginning with an executive summary covering the five dimensions; regulation follows the Better Regulation Framework.

items.title: Appraisal summary table (AST)
items.text: Recommended AST per shortlisted option: description (why preferred or inferior); summary metrics (NPSV, BCR, RPSC or NPUC); unmonetisable costs and benefits; public sector financial impact (nominal, undiscounted); distribution across groups and places; with risks and uncertainties for each element.

items.title: Monitoring and evaluation
items.text: Monitoring tracks delivery progress; evaluation assesses design, implementation and outcomes (Magenta Book). Goals: learning and accountability.

items.title: Types of evaluation
items.text: Process, impact and value for money evaluation.

items.title: Evaluation evidence as input
items.text: Use evaluation evidence for rationale, objectives and option appraisal, including historical forecast errors to derive optimism bias adjustments.

items.title: Evaluation plan
items.text: Develop an evaluation plan once a preferred option is identified and have a robust plan before final approval, based on the theory of change; the management case sets out monitoring and evaluation.

items.title: M&E costs included
items.text: Include M&E costs in the economic and financial dimensions; no fixed proportion, assess case by case.

items.title: Evaluation registry and business case publication
items.text: Register evaluations on the Government Evaluation Registry; GMPP business cases must be published within four months of HM Treasury approval.

items.title: Private finance at longlist
items.text: Use the Table A.1 qualitative questions alongside the CSFs to decide whether a private finance model should be the preferred way forward or shortlisted.

items.title: Private finance shortlist requirements
items.text: Include a public sector option (unless agreed with HM Treasury) and an additional sensitivity discounting the costs of all shortlisted options at the risk-free real gilt rate.

items.title: Model payments as they occur
items.text: Model private finance social costs as public-to-private payments over the contract as they occur, regardless of balance sheet classification.

items.title: Public sector option (comparator)
items.text: An equivalent-quality, publicly financed and procured option, adjusted for effective tax differences; optimism bias applied to all options.

items.title: Gilt-rate sensitivity
items.text: Discount only the costs of each shortlisted option at the risk-free real gilt rate matching the weighted average contract duration (consult HM Treasury for the rate; none is given in the Green Book).

stpr.description: Social Time Preference Rate (real). Year 0 is undiscounted (factor 1). The rate for year t applies to the step from year t-1 to t, so factors compound across bands.
stpr.note: The 2026 text states 2.50% 'for year 76 onwards' with no further step-down; earlier-edition schedules are not used.

health_discount_rate.applies: every year of the appraisal, to health and life effects only

table7_worked_example.description: Table 7 GDP deflator factors for years 0-5 at 2% general inflation (illustrative only).

time_horizons_years_after_year0.note: Agree a suitable period with HM Treasury if significant effects extend beyond 60 years (para 6.12).

welfare_weight_elasticity.formula: (median equivalised income of national population / median equivalised income of group) ^ 1.3

bcr_threshold.statement: No BCR threshold may be used to judge value for money.

not_in_edition.statement: Not given in the 2026 Green Book. Use the organisation's historical forecast errors, else generic values from the Green Book supplementary guidance on optimism bias (or departmental guidance, e.g. DfT). Must be supplied by the user.
